analysis: The method writeBytes takes a source byte array buff, offset off, and length len. It checks if the current position (pos) plus len exceeds the length of the internal array arr, and if so, resizes arr (calling resize). Then it calls System.arraycopy(buff, off, arr, pos, len). No null checks are performed on buff or arr, and no bounds checks on off, len, or pos (other than ensuring arr capacity). The arraycopy documentation lists three exception types: NullPointerException (if src or dest null), ArrayStoreException (type mismatches or non‑array objects), and IndexOutOfBoundsException (negative indices or length, or out‑of‑bounds source/destination ranges). Since both arrays are byte arrays, ArrayStoreException cannot occur due to type consistency. However, NullPointerException is not avoided because buff could be null and arr could be null (if not initialized). IndexOutOfBoundsException is not avoided because off could be negative, len could be negative, pos could be negative, or off+len could exceed buff.length — none of these are checked before the call.
answer: NullPointerException: NOT avoided (no null check on buff or arr). ArrayStoreException: AVOIDED (both arrays are byte[] so type mismatches cannot occur). IndexOutOfBoundsException: NOT avoided (no validation of off, len, pos, or source bounds).
remark: NullPointerException triggers if buff is null (since no null check) or if arr is null (though arr likely initialized, not guaranteed). IndexOutOfBoundsException triggers if off is negative, len is negative, pos is negative, or if off+len exceeds buff.length (no source bounds check). The destination bounds are safe due to the resize check (pos+len <= arr.length after resize).
